summary: Gérald Genta (1931-2011), Geneva-born designer, is credited with the Audemars Piguet Royal Oak and the Patek Philippe Nautilus (launched 1976). Sotheby's and Wikipedia both name him as designer; both describe the Royal Oak's diving-helmet inspiration. Sources disagree on the Royal Oak launch year, so no year is claimed for it.

sources.title: Gérald Genta: The Most Visionary Watch Designer of the 20th Century

claims.text: Gérald Genta was born in 1931 in Geneva and died in 2011.
claims.evidence: Sotheby's: 'born in 1931 in Geneva, Switzerland'; death in 2011. Wikipedia: 'Gérald Charles Genta (1 May 1931 – 17 August 2011)'.

claims.text: Genta designed the Audemars Piguet Royal Oak.
claims.evidence: Both sources list the Royal Oak among Genta's designs.

claims.text: The Royal Oak was inspired by vintage diving helmets and has exposed screws.
claims.evidence: Wikipedia: 'inspired by traditional diving helmets and therefore featured exposed screw heads'. Sotheby's: 'inspired by vintage diving helmets'.

claims.text: Genta designed the Patek Philippe Nautilus, introduced in 1976.
claims.evidence: Wikipedia: 'In 1976, Patek Philippe introduced the Nautilus collection, designed by Genta'. Sotheby's: the Nautilus 'debuted in 1976'.

claims.text: Genta designed the IWC Ingenieur, manufactured from 1976.
claims.evidence: Wikipedia: 'Designed by Gerald Genta in 1974 and manufactured by IWC Schaffhausen in 1976'. Sotheby's: the Ingenieur SL 'was also released in 1976'.

claims.text: Cartier invited Genta around 1985 to redesign the Pasha.
claims.evidence: Sotheby's: 'Around 1985, Cartier invited Genta to redesign an idiosyncratic watch'. Wikipedia lists 'Pasha de Cartier (1985)'.

gaps.description: Royal Oak launch year: Sotheby's says 1972, Wikipedia says 1970; not used.

analysis.conclusion: One designer, two steel sports icons: Genta is credited with the Royal Oak and the Nautilus, confirmed by Sotheby's and Wikipedia. Dates used only where both sources agree.
analysis.scope: Story behind Gérald Genta, from Sotheby's article and Wikipedia, read 2026-11-20.
